title: Threats Primer
scenario: Welcome to Threats Primer. Before proceeding, you must master these essential networking terms. Advanced Persistent Threat (APT): Sophisticated, long-term targeted attack, typically nation-state sponsored. Stealth over speed — establish foothold, maintain persistence, exfiltrate data over months/years. Hard to detect. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS): DoS using many compromised systems (botnet). Categories: Volumetric (DNS amplification), Protocol (SYN flood), Application (HTTP flood). Mitigated by scrubbing centers and rate limiting. Man-in-the-Middle (MITM): Attacker intercepts communication between two parties. Methods: ARP poisoning, rogue AP, DNS spoofing. Mitigated by encryption (TLS), certificate pinning, DAI, and 802.1X. Denial of Service (DoS): Attack overwhelming a target to make it unavailable. Single attacker. Types: volumetric (bandwidth), protocol (SYN flood), application (HTTP flood). DDoS = distributed (botnet).
question: What does APT stand for?
explanation: APT stands for Advanced Persistent Threat.
